ports.input: a 6-bit control signal for selecting the operation to be performed.
ports.output: a 32-bit output representing the result of the operation.
a 1-bit output indicating whether the result is zero.
a 1-bit output indicating whether a carry occurred during the operation.
a 1-bit output indicating whether the result is negative.
a 1-bit output indicating whether an overflow occurred during the operation.
a 1-bit output representing a general flag, which is set based on specific operations (SLT and SLTU).

logic_description.description: Notice that below descriptions are along with tags <logic />. With a <logic type="combinational_logic" />, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this <logic type="combinational_logic" /> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block. With a <logic type="sequential_logic" />, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other <logic type="sequential_logic" /> or <logic type="combinational_logic" /> states. With a <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description. With a <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation.
logic_description.logic: `zero` flag is active if `res` is all 0.
`carry` is equalled to the MSB of the `res` in cases `ADD`, `ADDU`, `SUB` , and `SUBU` alu opcodes. otherwise, `carry` is 0.

In case `ADD` ALU opcode, `overflow` is active if (MSB of `a` is deactive, MSB of `b` is deactive, and MSB of `r` is active) or (MSB of `a` is active, MSB of `b` is active, and MSB of `r` is deactive). In case `SUB` ALU opcode, `overflow` is active if (MSB of `a` is active, MSB of `b` is deactive, and MSB of `r` is deactive) or (MSB of `a` is deactive, MSB of `b` is deactive, and MSB of `r` is active). Otherwise, `overflow` is 0.
The output `r` is assigned to the first 32 bits of `res`.

The size of `res` is 33 bits. Operation result of all ALU opcodes. In case of `SLL`, `SRL`, and `SRA`, `res` is result of appropriate shift operations between all 32-bit `b` and all 32-bit `a`. In case of `SLLV`, `SRLV`, and `SRAV`, `res` is result of appropriate shift operations between 32-bit `b` and 5-bit `a`. Otherwise, `res` is the operation result normally from ADD, ADDU, SUB, SUBU, AND, OR, XOR, NOR, SLT, SLTU, and LUI.
`negative` is set to the MSB of the output `r`.

In case of `SLT` opcode, `flag` is active if 32-bit signed `a` is less than 32-bit signed `b`. In case of `SLTU` opcode, `flag` is active if 32-bit unsigned `a` is less than 32-bit unsigned `b`. Otherwise, `flag` is set to 0.

module.implementation: The module uses parameters to define the control signals for various operations, such as ADD, SUB, AND, OR, etc. The module assigns the input operands to the signed wires and the output result (r) to the lower 32 bits of the register (res[32:0]). The flag output is determined based on the control signal (aluc) and is set to '1' when the operation is SLT or SLTU, and '0' otherwise. The zero output is set to '1' when the result is all zeros, and '0' otherwise. Inside the always block, a case statement is used to perform the appropriate operation based on the control signal (aluc). The result is assigned to the register (res) accordingly. For the LUI operation, the upper 16 bits of 'a' are concatenated with 16 zeros to form the result. If the control signal (aluc) does not match any defined operation, the result is assigned as '0'. Please provide correct `Logic description` fields above to achieve correctness for `alu` design in combinational logics.
